```{r}
#| label: original-study
#| include: false

# The original study's numbers, entered once and used by the power analysis, the Key
# statistics table, and the side-by-side figures. Replace these with your original study's
# values, and say in a comment exactly where in the paper each one comes from.
#
# Stephens et al. (2012) — Study 3
# Design: 2 (social class: first-generation vs. continuing-generation) x 2 (condition: independent
# vs. interdependent welcome letter) between-subjects ANCOVA on the number of anagrams solved
# (out of 20, in 10 min), controlling for race (White/non-White) and self-reported high
# school GPA (p. 1190).
#
# Sample (pp. 1189-1190): N = 88 (42 first-gen, 46 continuing-gen).
# The four cell sizes are not reported.
#
# Results (p. 1190):
# No significant main effects (no statistics were reported).
# Social class x condition interaction was significant, F(1, 82) = 4.7, p = .03

# Social class x condition interaction
original_N   <- 88
original_F   <- 4.7
original_df1 <- 1
original_df2 <- 82    # = 88 - 4 cells - 2 covariates
original_p   <- .03

original_eta_p2 <- (original_F * original_df1) / (original_F * original_df1 + original_df2)
original_f      <- sqrt(original_eta_p2 / (1 - original_eta_p2))

# Cell means 
original <- tibble(
  social_class = c("first-gen", "first-gen", "continuing-gen", "continuing-gen"),
  condition    = c("independent", "interdependent", "independent", "interdependent"),
  mean         = c(6.9, 8.8, 9.2, 8.3),   # Figure 2 bar labels (adjusted means)
  se           = c(0.7, 0.6, 0.6, 0.7)    # Figure 2 error bars (these were visually estimated.. exact SEs weren't reported)
)

original_r_cov <- NA

# The key estimate on the anagram scale, the "difference of differences": how many more
# anagrams first-gen students solved relative to continuing-gen students with the
# interdependent letter than with the independent letter. From the Figure 2 means:
# (8.8 - 8.3) - (6.9 - 9.2) = 2.8. Its SE combines the four (visually estimated) cell SEs,
# so the interval built from it is approximate.
fg_inter <- original$mean[original$social_class == "first-gen" & original$condition == "interdependent"]
cg_inter <- original$mean[original$social_class == "continuing-gen" & original$condition == "interdependent"]
fg_ind   <- original$mean[original$social_class == "first-gen" & original$condition == "independent"]
cg_ind   <- original$mean[original$social_class == "continuing-gen" & original$condition == "independent"]
original_dod    <- (fg_inter - cg_inter) - (fg_ind - cg_ind)
original_dod_se <- sqrt(sum(original$se^2))
```

# Key statistics

```{r}
#| label: analysis-functions
#| code-summary: "Show the analysis code (shared by Phase 1 and Phase 2)"

# ---- Exclusion rules: EDIT to match your preregistration ---------------------------------
# Always applied, in this order (they define who can be analysed at all): consented,
# freshman (the inclusion criterion), reached the debrief, submitted at least one anagram answer, social class classifiable from
# the parental-education answers, and both covariates reported (the ANCOVA needs them).
# Optional rules: TRUE removes those participants; FALSE only reports the flag (see the
# screening table under Exploratory analyses).
exclude_if <- list(
  outside_help = FALSE  # answered "Yes" to using outside help on the anagrams
)

first_year <- "First-year (frosh)"  # only for Pilot A sessions recorded before the "Are you a freshman?" screen

# One answer from a SurveyJS response (a JSON string). NA when skipped or "Prefer not to say"
# (which SurveyJS stores as "none"). Multi-select answers are joined with ";".
answer <- function(json, key) {
  map_chr(json, function(j) {
    if (is.na(j) || j == "") return(NA_character_)
    v <- fromJSON(j, simplifyVector = TRUE)[[key]]
    if (is.null(v) || length(v) == 0 || identical(v, "none")) NA_character_ else paste(v, collapse = ";")
  })
}
declined <- function(json, key) str_detect(coalesce(answer(json, key), ""), "decline")

# Social class from the two parental-education answers (same rule as experiment.js):
# continuing-gen if any parent has a 4-year degree; first-gen if at least one parent's
# education is known and below a 4-year degree ("Don't know" / "Not applicable" for the other
# parent is ignored); NA (unclassifiable) if no parent's education is known.
four_year    <- c("bachelors", "graduate")
no_four_year <- c("less_than_hs", "high_school", "some_college", "associates")
classify_first_gen <- function(p1, p2) {
  case_when(p1 %in% four_year | p2 %in% four_year       ~ FALSE,
            p1 %in% no_four_year | p2 %in% no_four_year ~ TRUE,
            .default = NA)
}

# Load one phase's exported data and apply the exclusion rules. Returns NULL if that phase
# has not been exported yet, which is how every section below knows to skip itself.
read_phase <- function(id) {
  dir <- file.path("..", "data", "raw", id)
  if (!all(file.exists(file.path(dir, c("participants.csv", "trials.csv"))))) return(NULL)
  participants <- read_csv(file.path(dir, "participants.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 1e5)
  trials       <- read_csv(file.path(dir, "trials.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 1e5)
  errors_path  <- file.path(dir, "errors.csv")
  errors <- if (file.exists(errors_path)) read_csv(errors_path, show_col_types = FALSE) else tibble()

  # Participant-level fields saved by the experiment. A column is missing from exports made
  # before the field existed (e.g. `eligible` before the first-year screen was added).
  for (col in c("condition", "class_year", "eligible", "first_gen", "race_white_only",
                "outside_help", "anagrams_solved",
                "letter_time_ms", "letter_after_last_ms", "letter_max_scroll",
                "anagram_focus_losses")) {
    if (!col %in% names(participants)) participants[[col]] <- NA
  }
  reached <- function(task_name) unique(trials$participant_id[trials$task == task_name])
  consented <- trials |> filter(task == "consent", as.logical(consented)) |> pull(participant_id)
  # "Attempted" = submitted at least one answer (skips and time-outs alone do not count).
  attempted <- if ("action" %in% names(trials)) {
    trials |> filter(task == "anagram", action == "submit") |> pull(participant_id) |> unique()
  } else character(0)

  demo <- trials |>
    filter(task == "demographics") |>
    transmute(participant_id,
              hs_gpa = if_else(declined(response, "hs_gpa_decline"), NA_real_,
                               suppressWarnings(as.numeric(answer(response, "hs_gpa")))),
              hs_gpa_scale = answer(response, "hs_gpa_scale"),
              age = if_else(declined(response, "age_decline"), NA_real_,
                            suppressWarnings(as.numeric(answer(response, "age")))),
              gender = answer(response, "gender"),
              sex = answer(response, "sex"),
              race = answer(response, "race"),
              household_income = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(answer(response, "household_income"))),
              parent1_education = answer(response, "parent1_education"),
              parent2_education = answer(response, "parent2_education")) |>
    distinct(participant_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

  d <- participants |>
    left_join(demo, by = "participant_id") |>
    mutate(eligible        = coalesce(as.logical(eligible), class_year == first_year),
           # Recomputed from the raw answers so every session uses the same rule; the value
           # saved by the browser is used only if the answers are missing.
           first_gen       = coalesce(classify_first_gen(parent1_education, parent2_education),
                                      as.logical(first_gen)),
           social_class    = factor(if_else(first_gen, "first-gen", "continuing-gen"),
                                    levels = c("first-gen", "continuing-gen")),
           condition       = factor(condition, levels = c("independent", "interdependent")),
           race_white      = as.numeric(as.logical(race_white_only)),
           anagrams_solved = as.numeric(anagrams_solved))

  rules <- list(
    "Started"                          = rep(TRUE, nrow(d)),
    "Consented"                        = d$participant_id %in% consented,
    "Freshman (inclusion criterion)"   = d$eligible %in% TRUE,
    "Completed the study"              = d$participant_id %in% reached("debrief"),
    "Attempted at least one anagram"   = d$participant_id %in% attempted,
    "Social class classifiable"        = !is.na(d$first_gen),
    "Covariates reported (race, GPA)"  = !is.na(d$race_white) & !is.na(d$hs_gpa)
  )
  if (isTRUE(exclude_if$outside_help))   rules[["No outside help"]] <- !(d$outside_help %in% "Yes")
  # Each step keeps the participants who pass it and every earlier step.
  passed <- setNames(accumulate(rules, `&`), names(rules))

  list(participants = participants, trials = trials, errors = errors, d = d,
       rules = rules, passed = passed, keep = d[passed[[length(passed)]], ])
}

covariates_with_variance <- function(dd) {
  c("race_white", "hs_gpa")[map_lgl(c("race_white", "hs_gpa"), ~ n_distinct(dd[[.x]]) > 1)]
}

# The key analysis: 2 (social class) x 2 (letter) between-subjects ANCOVA on anagrams solved,
# covariates race (White vs not) and high school GPA, Type III tests (as in SPSS, the usual
# software for an ANCOVA reported this way). Both factors are coded -1/2 and +1/2, so the
# interaction coefficient is the difference of differences on the anagram scale:
#   (first-gen minus continuing-gen, interdependent) - (first-gen minus continuing-gen, independent)
# Returns NULL until every cell has at least 2 participants. A covariate with no variation
# (possible in a tiny pilot) is left out, and `covariates` records which were used.
fit_ancova <- function(keep) {
  if (is.null(keep) || nrow(keep) == 0) return(NULL)
  cells <- count(keep, social_class, condition, .drop = FALSE)
  if (nrow(cells) < 4 || any(cells$n < 2)) return(NULL)
  dd <- keep |> mutate(class_c = if_else(social_class == "first-gen", 0.5, -0.5),
                       cond_c  = if_else(condition == "interdependent", 0.5, -0.5))
  covs <- covariates_with_variance(dd)
  m <- lm(reformulate(c("class_c * cond_c", covs), response = "anagrams_solved"), data = dd)
  if (df.residual(m) < 1) return(NULL)
  a <- car::Anova(m, type = 3)
  term <- "class_c:cond_c"
  grid <- expand_grid(social_class = factor(levels(keep$social_class), levels = levels(keep$social_class)),
                      condition    = factor(levels(keep$condition), levels = levels(keep$condition))) |>
    mutate(class_c = if_else(social_class == "first-gen", 0.5, -0.5),
           cond_c  = if_else(condition == "interdependent", 0.5, -0.5),
           race_white = mean(dd$race_white), hs_gpa = mean(dd$hs_gpa))
  pr <- predict(m, newdata = grid, se.fit = TRUE)  # adjusted (estimated marginal) means
  list(model = m, anova = a, covariates = covs, N = nrow(dd), cells = cells,
       F = a[term, "F value"], df1 = 1, df2 = a["Residuals", "Df"], p = a[term, "Pr(>F)"],
       eta_p2 = a[term, "F value"] / (a[term, "F value"] + a["Residuals", "Df"]),
       estimate = unname(coef(m)[term]),
       ci_low = confint(m)[term, 1], ci_high = confint(m)[term, 2],
       sigma = sigma(m),
       means = grid |> transmute(social_class, condition, mean = pr$fit, se = pr$se.fit))
}

# Follow-up tests reported in the original (p. 1190): the social class gap within each
# letter, and the letter effect within each social class, each an ANCOVA with the covariates.
simple_effects <- function(keep) {
  run <- function(sub, term, label) {
    sub <- droplevels(sub)
    if (nrow(sub) < 4 || n_distinct(sub[[term]]) < 2) return(NULL)
    m <- lm(reformulate(c(term, covariates_with_variance(sub)), response = "anagrams_solved"), data = sub)
    if (df.residual(m) < 1) return(NULL)
    a <- car::Anova(m, type = 3)
    tibble(Test = label, `F` = a[term, "F value"], df = sprintf("(1, %d)", a["Residuals", "Df"]),
           p = a[term, "Pr(>F)"])
  }
  bind_rows(
    map(levels(keep$condition), ~ run(filter(keep, condition == .x), "social_class",
                                      paste0("Social class gap, ", .x, " letter"))),
    map(levels(keep$social_class), ~ run(filter(keep, social_class == .x), "condition",
                                         paste0("Letter effect, ", .x, " students")))
  )
}

# Side-by-side figure: adjusted mean anagrams solved (+/- 1 SE, the original Figure 2's error
# bars) by social class and letter, one panel per study, same axes and colours as the original.
# Until the ANCOVA can run (every cell needs at least 2 participants), the replication panel
# shows unadjusted cell means instead, +/- 1 SE where a cell has 2 or more people, with n.
raw_means <- function(keep) {
  if (is.null(keep) || nrow(keep) == 0) return(NULL)
  keep |>
    group_by(social_class, condition, .drop = FALSE) |>
    summarise(n = n(), mean = if (n > 0) mean(anagrams_solved) else NA_real_,
              se = if (n > 1) sd(anagrams_solved) / sqrt(n) else NA_real_, .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(mean = ifelse(n > 0, mean, NA_real_))
}

# APA 7 figure style: white background, no gridlines, black axis lines and ticks, sans-serif
# text, grayscale bars with black outlines, title-case axis labels, legend without a title.
apa_theme <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
          axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black"),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
          axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
          axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)),
          legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank(),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.9, "lines"),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(size = base_size, face = "plain"),
          panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"),
          plot.margin = margin(6, 12, 6, 6))
}

# Side-by-side figure: mean anagrams solved (+/- 1 SE, the original Figure 2's error bars) by
# social class and letter, one panel per study, same axes. Where a study's rows carry `n`
# (the unadjusted fallback), each bar is labelled with its n.
comparison_plot <- function(...) {
  studies <- list(...)
  studies <- studies[!map_lgl(studies, is.null)]
  df <- imap_dfr(studies, ~ mutate(.x, Study = .y)) |>
    mutate(Study = factor(Study, levels = names(studies)),
           social_class = factor(social_class, levels = c("first-gen", "continuing-gen"),
                                 labels = c("First-generation", "Continuing-generation")),
           condition = factor(condition, levels = c("independent", "interdependent"),
                              labels = c("Independent", "Interdependent")))
  if (!"n" %in% names(df)) df$n <- NA_integer_
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.8, preserve = "single")  # an empty cell leaves a gap
  ggplot(df, aes(x = condition, y = mean, fill = social_class)) +
    geom_col(position = dodge, width = 0.75, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), position = dodge,
                  width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(aes(y = 0.4, label = ifelse(is.na(n), "", sprintf("n = %d", n)), colour = social_class),
              position = dodge, vjust = 0, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("First-generation" = "black", "Continuing-generation" = "white")) +
    facet_wrap(~ Study, nrow = 1) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 20, 4), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 20)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("First-generation" = "#D9D9D9", "Continuing-generation" = "#5A5A5A")) +
    labs(x = "Welcome Letter", y = "Number of Anagrams Solved") +
    apa_theme()
}

phase1 <- read_phase(experiment_id)
phase2 <- read_phase(experiment_id_phase2)
have_data   <- !is.null(phase1)
have_phase2 <- !is.null(phase2)
res1 <- if (have_data) fit_ancova(phase1$keep)
res2 <- if (have_phase2) fit_ancova(phase2$keep)
```

```{r}
#| label: key-stats

fmt_row <- function(study, r) {
  if (is.null(r)) {
    return(tibble(Study = study, N = "", `Interaction F` = "not enough data yet", `Partial η²` = "",
                  `Difference of differences [95% CI]` = "", p = ""))
  }
  tibble(Study = study, N = as.character(r$N),
         `Interaction F` = sprintf("F(%d, %d) = %.2f", r$df1, r$df2, r$F),
         `Partial η²` = sprintf("%.3f", r$eta_p2),
         `Difference of differences [95% CI]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]", r$estimate, r$ci_low, r$ci_high),
         p = format.pval(r$p, digits = 2, eps = 0.001))
}
original_row <- list(N = original_N, df1 = original_df1, df2 = original_df2, F = original_F,
                     eta_p2 = original_eta_p2, estimate = original_dod, p = original_p,
                     ci_low = original_dod - 1.96 * original_dod_se,
                     ci_high = original_dod + 1.96 * original_dod_se)
bind_rows(
  fmt_row("Original", original_row),
  fmt_row("Phase 1: replication", res1),
  fmt_row("Phase 2: extension", res2)
) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrlrlr",
               caption = "Key comparison: Social Class × Condition interaction on anagrams solved (ANCOVA with race and high school GPA as covariates). Difference of differences: how many more anagrams first-generation students solved relative to continuing-generation students with the interdependent letter than with the independent letter. The original's interval is approximate, because its SEs were read off Figure 2.")
```

# Phase 1: Replication

## Introduction

Despite increases in higher education social class diversity,
first-generation college students (students whose parents do not have a
bachelor's degree or higher) continue to lag behind their
continuing-generation peers in terms of academic achievement and degree
completion. Stephens et al.'s (2012) cultural mismatch theory proposes
that the academic achievement gap is in part due to a cultural match or
mismatch between a students' upbringing and the norms perpetuated in the
larger university context. Study 3 experimentally tested whether a
cultural match or mismatch between students' motives for college and
university norms impacted performance in a verbal academic task.
Supporting cultural mismatch theory, the authors found a significant
interaction between social class (first-generation,
continuing-generation) and condition (interdependent, independent). When
the university norms are framed with independence messaging (e.g.,
finding your passion), first-generation students performed significantly
worse than continuing-generation students in the verbal reasoning task.
However, when the university norms are framed with interdependence
messaging (e.g., giving back to your family), first-generation students
performed just as well on the task as their continuing-generation peers.
The results of this study suggests that a small change in the
university's cultural framing may foster appreciation of multiple
cultural models of self and promote positive performance among first-generation college students.


## Methods

### Power analysis

```{r}
#| label: power
n_cells      <- 4
n_covariates <- 2
planned_first_gen_share <- 0.20  # EDIT: expected share of first-generation students in your sample

# With unequal groups the interaction is estimated less precisely than with four equal cells.
# Its variance is proportional to the sum of 1/n over the cells, so with a share q of
# first-gen students (and the letter split 50/50) the required N grows by this factor:
imbalance <- function(q) (1 / q + 1 / (1 - q)) / 4

power_rows <- map_dfr(c(0.80, 0.90, 0.95), function(pw) {
  v <- pwr::pwr.f2.test(u = original_df1, f2 = original_f^2, sig.level = 0.05, power = pw)$v
  n_equal <- ceiling(v) + n_cells + n_covariates   # total N = v + 4 cells + 2 covariates
  tibble(power = scales::percent(pw), n_equal = n_equal,
         n_unequal = ceiling(n_equal * imbalance(planned_first_gen_share)))
})
two_and_half <- ceiling(2.5 * original_N)

knitr::kable(power_rows,
             col.names = c("Power", "N total, four equal cells",
                           sprintf("N total, %.0f%% first-gen (approx.)", 100 * planned_first_gen_share)),
             caption = sprintf(
               "Sample needed to detect the original Social Class × Condition interaction (F(1, %d) = %.1f, partial η² = %.3f, Cohen's f = %.2f) in a 2 × 2 ANCOVA with %d covariates, two-sided α = .05. The right-hand column scales the equal-cell N by %.2f for unequal groups. 2.5 times the original sample is %d.",
               original_df2, original_F, original_eta_p2, original_f, n_covariates,
               imbalance(planned_first_gen_share), two_and_half))
```

The original effect size is partial η² = .054, f = 0.24. The N for 80% power is 143 for equal groups and 224 for unequal groups (20% first-generation students). 

### Planned sample

My ideal sample size is 224, based on 80% power of the original study's effect size and adjusted for potentially unequal groups. This is roughly equivalent to the alternative calculation of 2.5 times the original sample size to detect an effect the original study had only 33% power to detect (N = 220). I plan to stop collecting data once 224 participants who meet the study criteria complete the study. The sampling frame is first-year (freshman) Stanford students who are 18 or older and enrolled in the Psych 1 course. Given that the Fall 2026 course enrollment is approximately 248, I anticipate that it would be highly unlikely for me to reach my ideal sample size. Therefore, I plan to continue recruiting participants in the second part of this replication project from the same participant pool until 11/02/2026. I will analyze the data that I have. I cannot collect data from Prolific because certain elements in the welcome letter require institution-specific information (e.g., name of university, current President information).

### Materials

#### Welcome letter
In the original study, participants read one of two (interdependent, independent) welcome letters that were printed on two pages. These welcome letters were adapted to be relevant to current year (2026) in an online format. This involved updating the Stanford President's name, background, photograph, and signature. 

Following the feedback of one of my Pilot A participants, I integrated interactive website elements (e.g., key text were presented one line at a time prompted with the "Show Next" button) to increase participant engagement. Following Pilot B, I restyled the progress bar to show a percentage, disabled question auto-advance ("Next" required on every question), and recorded the time participants spent per question.

#### Anagrams
The original study also included a hard copy anagram task. Since the task content and answer key were not provided in authors' supplemental materials, I used Gilhooly's (1978) list of five-letter single-solution anagrams. To mimic the hard copy format, I allowed participants to skip through words, with the opportunity to come back to them at a later time. Other aspects of the anagram task, such as the instructions that came before ("[We'd] like you to complete and evaluate an activity that has been used in the past with incoming students. The task’s purpose is to assess different learning styles"), duration (10 minutes), and number of anagrams (20) were aligned with the original study's implementation. I requested original materials to the corresponding author on 10/16/2026. The author has not responded (as of 10/24/2026). 

Since Pilot B participants solved 17, 18, and 11 out of the 20 anagrams, which was greater than original study's solve rate of approximately 8 out of 20 (based on the average of the four cell means), I increased the difficulty of anagrams by swapping six words that all six participants (across Pilots A and B) solved correctly with words in Gilhooly's (1978) list with a greater BR score (associated with anagram difficulty). I ensured that several easier anagrams were retained to prevent floor effects. As a result, I increased the average BR score of the anagram task from 56 (Pilot A and B) to 80 (Phase 1).

### Procedure

Interested first-year students enrolled in Psych 1 will sign-up for the study via the SONA platform and be directed to the online study website. If students are on a phone or tablet, they will be told to switch to a desktop or laptop. Once they are on a desktop or laptop, they will indicate whether they agree to participate. If they agree to participate, the next screen will ask whether they "Are a freshman" to confirm eligibility. If they answer anything other than "Yes," they will be thanked for their interest and asked to close the browser window. Participants who self-verify their first-year status will be randomly assigned one of the two welcome letters (interdependent, independent). Participants will be prompted to click "Show next" after a chunk of the letter is shown, with a 45-second minimum duration on the welcome letter page before participants can proceed to the next page. Afterwards, they will read about the next task's purpose and instructions for completing the anagrams. Participants will be given 10 minutes to complete as many anagrams as possible. They will be shown a maximum of 20 anagrams; one anagram at a time in a random order; and are allowed to skip. The anagram task will show a 10-minute countdown timer. Once the time is up, or if every anagram was answered before time ran out, they are thanked and asked to click "Continue." The next set of questions will cover the manipulation checks and their demographic information. The final question will ask whether participants used any outside help on the anagrams. Following this screen, participants will be shown the debriefing message and thanked for participating. This study will approximately take 15 minutes to complete.

### Analysis plan

**Key analysis of interest.** The number of anagrams solved will depend on the interaction between social class (first-generation vs. continuing-generation) and condition (interdependent vs. independent) tested with a 2 X 2 ANCOVA (Type III), controlling for race (White vs. non-White) and self-reported unweighted high school GPA. The effect sizes will be the difference of differences with 95% CI and partial η².

**Additional analyses.** Four one-way ANCOVAs within each level of the other factor, controlling for race (White/non-White) and self-reported high school GPA: (1) interdependent letter subset testing social class factor, (2) independent letter subset testing social class factor, (3) first-generation student subset testing condition factor, (4) continuing-generation student subset testing condition factor. Independent samples t-tests on the two manipulation check items.

**Exclusions.** Participants will be excluded if they did not consent; they are not freshman; they did not attempt any anagrams; they did not complete the study; they did not report their race/ethnicity; they did not report high school GPA; or their social class is not classifiable (i.e., answering "Don't know" for one parent's highest level of education and "Not Applicable" for the other parent's or answering "Don't know" to both parents' highest level of education).

### Differences from the original study

| Aspect | Original study | This replication | Expected to matter? |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Sample | First-year students in Stanford | First-year students in Stanford taking Psych 1 | Unlikely. However, limited pool of participants may not allow target sample size to be reached. Psych 1 students may have prior exposure to cultural mismatch theory. |
| Year | 2010-2011 | 2026 | May potentially diminish effect of cultural mismatch condition given more support for first-generation college students. |
| Setting | In-person, with experimenter | Online, unsupervised, on the participant's own computer | Possibly; attention may be lower online and outside help may be used to complete task. |
| President's name and information | "John L. Hennessy" and handwritten signature | "Jonathan Levin" and name in script typeface for signature | Unlikely. |
| Format of welcome message | Two printed pages | One screen; "Show next" reveals next chunk of information, one click at a time | Possibly, attention may be lower online. |
| Anagram items | 20 anagrams, not published | 20 anagrams from Gilhooly (1978) | Possibly, given unknown difficulty level of original anagrams. |
| Anagram responses | Writing on paper | Typing on screen | Unlikely, but may reduce engagement |
| Cover story | Spoken by experimenter | Shown on screen | Unlikely, but may reduce engagement. |

```{r}
  done <- pilot$passed[["Completed the study"]]
  funnel_pilot <- tibble(Step = c("Opened the study", "Turned away (phone or tablet)", names(pilot$passed)[-1]),
         N = c(nrow(pd), sum(!as.logical(pd$device_supported) %in% TRUE),
               map_int(pilot$passed[-1], sum))) |>
    knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Pilot B: participants remaining after each step (steps apply in order). Median time to complete: %.1f minutes.",
                                   median(pd$minutes[done], na.rm = TRUE)))
  completers_pilot <- pd[done, ] |>
    transmute(Letter = str_to_sentence(as.character(condition)),
              `Social class` = recode(as.character(social_class), `first-gen` = "First-generation",
                                      `continuing-gen` = "Continuing-generation", .missing = "Unclassifiable"),
              `Anagrams solved (of 20)` = anagrams_solved,
              `Anagrams skipped` = as.numeric(anagram_skips),
              `Seconds on letter` = round(as.numeric(letter_time_ms) / 1000),
              Minutes = round(minutes, 1)) |>
    arrange(Letter, `Social class`) |>
    knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Pilot B completers (n = %d), on the pilot anagram set (mean Gilhooly BR 56; replaced afterwards by the final set, mean BR 80). Mean solved: %.1f of 20 (%.0f%%); the original's cell means imply about 8 of 20.",
                                   sum(done), mean(pd$anagrams_solved[done], na.rm = TRUE),
                                   5 * mean(pd$anagrams_solved[done], na.rm = TRUE)))
  print(funnel_pilot)
  print(completers_pilot)
} else {
  message("No Pilot B export found under data/raw/", pilot_id, ".")
}
```
Three participants provided consent and completed Pilot B (median completion time of 13.3 minutes). The number of completed surveys matched the number of participants who signed up for the study through SONA. They provided all the key information for analyses and there was no missing data.

### Exploratory analyses

```{r}
#| label: manipulation-check
#| eval: !expr have_data
# Manipulation check (p. 1190): two 1-7 ratings, compared between letters with Student's t tests
# as in the original. "Prefer not to say" is missing here.
mc <- trials |>
  filter(task == "manipulation_check", participant_id %in% keep$participant_id) |>
  select(participant_id, any_of(c("mc_individually_motivated", "mc_work_together"))) |>
  left_join(select(keep, participant_id, condition), by = "participant_id")
mc_test <- function(item, label, original_text) {
  if (!item %in% names(mc)) return(NULL)
  x <- mc |> filter(!is.na(.data[[item]]))
  g <- split(x[[item]], x$condition)
  ok <- length(g) == 2 && all(lengths(g) >= 2)
  tt <- if (ok) t.test(g$independent, g$interdependent, var.equal = TRUE)
  ms <- function(v) if (length(v) == 0) "—" else if (length(v) == 1) sprintf("%.1f, n = 1", v) else
    sprintf("%.1f (%.1f), n = %d", mean(v), sd(v), length(v))
  tibble(Item = label,
         Independent = ms(g$independent),
         Interdependent = ms(g$interdependent),
         t = if (ok) sprintf("t(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f", tt$parameter, tt$statistic, tt$p.value) else "not enough data",
         Original = original_text)
}
tab_mc <- bind_rows(
  mc_test("mc_individually_motivated", "Be individually motivated", "6.6 (0.6) vs 6.1 (0.9), t(86) = 3.2"),
  mc_test("mc_work_together", "Work together with other students", "5.6 (1.3) vs 6.1 (0.8), t(86) = −2.2")
)
if (nrow(mc) > 0 && nrow(tab_mc) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(tab_mc, caption = "Manipulation check: mean (SD) agreement, 1–7, that the university expects each, by letter.")
} else {
  message("No manipulation-check answers from analysed participants yet.")
}
```

## Discussion

### Summary of replication attempt

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Guidance

Open with one paragraph summarizing the result of the key analysis and
your assessment of whether the original finding replicated, partially
replicated, or failed to replicate. Base that judgment on the
replication assessment above: the size of the effect relative to the
original, not just the p value.
:::

### Commentary

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Guidance

Open-ended commentary, none of it long: (a) what the exploratory
analyses suggest; (b) what the replication means, for example whether
the differences between your study and the original are definitely,
plausibly, or unlikely to be moderators of the result; and (c) any
objections or challenges raised by you or the original authors.
:::

# Phase 2: Extension

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Guidance: choosing your extension

Follow the Extension guidelines page on Canvas. In brief:

-   **By default the extension is a best-practices modification of your
    Phase 1 experiment.** If your replication did not succeed, it is a
    **rescue**: address the plausible reasons for the failure. If it did
    succeed, it is an **upgrade**: make the estimate more precise.
    Typical changes are better or more reliable measurement, more
    trials, a within-participant design where that is legitimate,
    comprehension and manipulation checks, clearer instructions, or a
    larger or better-targeted sample.
-   **If your scientific extension pitch was approved at Milestone 3 and
    your replication succeeded, propose that instead:** the original
    conditions rerun unchanged, plus the one added condition or
    manipulation, with a power analysis for the new comparison.
-   On either track you may add exploratory measures **at the end** of
    the study.
-   Every change is listed and tagged by category below; everything else
    stays identical.

State your track on the line below, and delete the others.
:::

**Track:** Best-practices upgrade / Best-practices rescue / Scientific
extension (approved at Milestone 3)

## Rationale

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Guidance

One or two paragraphs. For a rescue: what are the plausible reasons
Phase 1 did not reproduce the original result, and how does each change
address one of them? For an upgrade: where is the Phase 1 estimate least
precise or least trustworthy, and how will the changes improve it? For a
scientific extension: what question does the added condition answer, and
why does it follow from the original finding?
:::

## Changes from Phase 1

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Guidance

Every change from the Phase 1 experiment, one per row, each tagged with
a category: Measurement, Trials, Design, Checks, Instructions, Sample,
Added condition (scientific track only), or Exploratory measure (end of
study only). If it is not in this table, it does not change: same
materials, wording, procedure, exclusion rule and analysis. The rows
below are examples for the demo; replace them with yours.
:::

| \# | Category | Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Why |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| 1 | Sample | 27 analysed participants | 300 analysed participants (150 per frame) | Phase 1's interval was too wide to distinguish the original effect from a much smaller one. |
| 2 | Checks | No comprehension check | After the choice, participants say how many people are at risk (600) | Confirms participants read the scenario; failures are reported, and excluded only if preregistered. |
| 3 | Exploratory measure | None | At the end: "How confident are you in your choice?" (1–7) | Exploratory only; collected after every confirmatory measure. |

Everything not listed above is identical to Phase 1.

## Power and sample

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Guidance

Justify the Phase 2 sample, and **state how you expect the estimate and
its precision to compare with Phase 1**. For an upgrade, plan the sample
around the confidence interval you want; for a rescue, around the power
to detect the original effect, or the smallest effect you would still
consider a successful replication; for a scientific extension, around
the power to detect the new comparison. Set `phase2_n_per_group` in the
code below; the table uses Phase 1's estimate if you have it and the
original's otherwise.
:::

```{r}
#| label: phase2-power
phase2_n_total <- 300   # planned analysed participants in Phase 2 (all four cells together)

# Effect and residual SD to plan around: Phase 1's if available, otherwise the original's
# (its residual SD is approximated from the Figure 2 SEs: SE x sqrt(n per cell)).
basis_f2 <- if (!is.null(res1)) res1$eta_p2 / (1 - res1$eta_p2) else original_f^2
basis_sd <- if (!is.null(res1)) res1$sigma else mean(original$se) * sqrt(original_N / n_cells)
basis_source <- if (!is.null(res1)) "Phase 1" else "the original study"

# Expected 95% CI half-width of the difference of differences, and power, at N total with a
# share q of first-gen students: the interaction's variance is sigma^2 x sum(1/n) over cells.
half_width <- function(n, q) 1.96 * basis_sd * sqrt((4 / n) * (1 / q + 1 / (1 - q)))
power_at <- function(n, f2, q) {
  v <- n - n_cells - n_covariates
  if (v < 1) return(NA)
  pwr::pwr.f2.test(u = 1, v = v, f2 = f2 / imbalance(q), sig.level = 0.05)$power
}

tibble(
  Study = c(if (!is.null(res1)) "Phase 1 (actual)", "Phase 2 (planned)"),
  `N analysed` = c(if (!is.null(res1)) res1$N, phase2_n_total),
  `95% CI half-width` = c(if (!is.null(res1)) sprintf("±%.1f anagrams", (res1$ci_high - res1$ci_low) / 2),
                          sprintf("±%.1f anagrams (expected)", half_width(phase2_n_total, planned_first_gen_share)))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Precision of the key estimate (difference of differences); Phase 2 expected value based on %s, with %.0f%% first-generation students.", basis_source, 100 * planned_first_gen_share))

tibble(
  `Effect to detect` = c(sprintf("Original: partial η² = %.3f", original_eta_p2),
                         if (!is.null(res1)) sprintf("Phase 1: partial η² = %.3f", res1$eta_p2),
                         "Half the original (Cohen's f halved)"),
  `Power at planned N` = scales::percent(c(
    power_at(phase2_n_total, original_f^2, planned_first_gen_share),
    if (!is.null(res1)) power_at(phase2_n_total, basis_f2, planned_first_gen_share),
    power_at(phase2_n_total, (original_f / 2)^2, planned_first_gen_share)
  ), accuracy = 1)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Power of the Phase 2 key test at N = %d, two-sided α = .05.", phase2_n_total))
```
